html:
The Bidjara are an Aboriginal Australian people of central southern Queensland, in the country around the headwaters of the Warrego River and the Carnarvon Range. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Carnarvon Gorge, a deep sandstone gorge in this region, holds some of the best known Aboriginal rock art in Queensland, with walls covered in stencils of hands, tools and weapons. The Bidjara language is one of the better recorded of the area, and several neighbouring peoples spoke related forms of it. Neighbours on the map include the Nguri, the Gunggari and the Garingbal. Squatters moved in from the 1850s and 1860s. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
